A rather shallow article. If they'd at least mention what kind of DLC is included in the various different editions and what all the different DLC consists of it might help the reader to form a better opinion. Without looking into it (I don't really care for the game), I gotta say though that I don't really consider "a deck of playing cards, a 14-inch statue, a messenger pigeon tube, a cloth poster" to be essential to get the full experience out of a game. Now if the remaining exclusive DLC is stuff like different skins, or re-skinned weapons that are the same as one of the base guns, etc., then I don't really need that either. If people want to spend money on that, that's cool, but I'm usually good with the base game.

The practice isn't as recent as the author (and many others) make it out to be either. BF2, arguably one of the best and well-praised games of the genre, had plenty of (rather expensive) DLC, they were just called expansion packs back in the day and very few people actually owned them. In a way that practice often has the developers shoot themselves in their foot too, because it fragments the player base which is always bad for a multiplayer game. In BF2's case the various expansion packs did little to take away from the solid base game experience which had a strong community for years, so you really didn't miss out on much by not buying that. It might be similar here.

Tl:Dr; Exclusive DLC isn't necessarily inherently terrible. Many games pull it off well where you can choose to pre-order or buy cosmetic DLC (like skins, whatever) which I wouldn't consider to be absolutely necessary for the "full experience" and it's a way for people to support the developers if they want to (do whatever you feel like with your money, it's none of my business). That's not to say that it cannot be abused to chop up what most people would really consider to be the full experience into separate, expensive bits of DLC, and that may very well be the case with Battlefield 1 (again, I haven't bothered to look into what the various DLC consists of), but either way that article is garbage if it doesn't even touch on that.
